subject: VM scan cadence: confirmed remediation tempo and temporary scan-gap mitigation
messages:
From: Audrey Liao <audrey.liao@monetbank.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: Daniel Huang <security@monetbank.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: latest VM cadence & remediation commitments for SOC2 evidence

Hi Camila,

Thanks for taking this. As part of MonetBank's annual SOC 2 refresh we're capturing third-party vendor vulnerability management proof. Can you provide:

- Current authenticated + unauthenticated external scan cadence (frequency and tooling)
- SLA windows you commit to for High / Medium / Low CVEs (days to remediation and verification)
- Any recent exceptions (temporary compensating controls) and a mitigation timeline for closure
- A single CSV or index of the last three months of scan artifacts (scan id, date, critical/high findings, disposition)

We need a documented attestation we can share with our auditor next Tuesday (2028-05-28). If there are any CVEs with extended remediation windows, please point them out and include owner and plan.

Appreciate a concise pack.

Best,
Audrey
Audrey Liao
Senior Information Security Manager | MonetBank

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Audrey Liao <audrey.liao@monetbank.com>
Cc: Daniel Huang <security@monetbank.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest VM cadence & remediation commitments for SOC2 evidence

Hi Audrey — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, and I'll attach the index and timeline:

- Scan cadence: External authenticated scans weekly (AstraScan), external unauthenticated scans nightly (OpenVAS->validation pipeline), container image SCA on every push (Clair-based), dependency SCA on CI per branch.
- SLAs: High = 30 days to remediation + verification; Medium = 90 days; Low = 180 days. Those map to our SOC2 commitments and are tracked in the remediation queue (JIRA-SEC-4892).
- Exceptions: We currently have a temporary exception for a legacy HA router appliance (CVE-2024-XY89) that cannot be hotpatched; compensating control = network segmentation + monitored IDS rules. Owner: Ben Carter (Network Security). Closure plan attached; projected closure by 2028-08-15.
- Attached: redwood-vm-scan-index-20280520.csv (last 3 months, index), CVE-2024-XY89-mitigation-plan-DR-20280521.pdf, scan-gap-review-notes-20280523.txt

I'll follow up with Marissa for a formal attestation note for your auditor. If you need a sign-off from our Head of Security, we can include Laura's endorsement this week.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Partner Security Manager | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Audrey Liao <audrey.liao@monetbank.com>, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest VM cadence & remediation commitments for SOC2 evidence

Audrey — pinging with a short attestation draft below you can share with your auditor. Camila, Ben: please confirm wording for the exception and closure date.

--- Attestation Draft ---
Redwood Inference attests that:
1) We operate a layered vulnerability management program including automated external authenticated scans (weekly), unauthenticated external scans (nightly), continuous container image scanning at build-time, and dependency/software composition analysis in CI/CD pipelines.
2) Our standard remediation SLAs are: High — 30 calendar days; Medium — 90 calendar days; Low — 180 calendar days. SLA performance is monitored and reported to our security ops dashboard.
3) Open exceptions are documented with compensating controls and assigned owners. At the time of this attestation there is one documented exception for a legacy router appliance (CVE-2024-XY89) with documented network segmentation mitigations and 24/7 IDS monitoring. The mitigation plan projects closure by 2028-08-15.

Please let us know if you need the attestation on letterhead or with Laura's signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Security Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
---

From: Daniel Huang <security@monetbank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: Audrey Liao <audrey.liao@monetbank.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest VM cadence & remediation commitments for SOC2 evidence

Marissa / Camila — thank you for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple clarifying points from our auditor's checklist:

1) Can you confirm how you triage scanner false positives (process + expected verification window after a scan)?
2) For CVE-2024-XY89: auditor wants evidence of the active compensating controls (network ACL exports, IDS rule IDs, and monitoring alert examples). Can you provide a masked set of logs or screenshots?
3) Are any of the remediation SLAs contractual (i.e., in a published SOC2 vendor statement) or internal policy only?

If you can forward the additional artifacts by EOD Friday (2028-05-25) that would be ideal.

Cheers,
Daniel
Security Engineer | MonetBank

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Daniel Huang <security@monetbank.com>, Audrey Liao <audrey.liao@monetbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest VM cadence & remediation commitments for SOC2 evidence

Daniel — thanks for the checklist. Quick response and attached artifacts (see Drive link):

1) False-positive triage: Scans are ingested into our remediation pipeline where triage owners (Security Ops) validate findings within 72 hours. Validation actions are recorded in JIRA ticket comments; if a finding is a false positive it is marked with "fp-confirmed" and closed with notes. The typical verification window post-scan is 72 hours for triage and 10 business days for a final disposition before SLA countdown begins (we treat verification as part of SLA for complex infra exceptions).

2) CVE-2024-XY89 artifacts: we provided a redacted ACL export (Drive), IDS rule IDs (IDS-7893, IDS-7894) and a sample monitoring alert screenshot (redacted). See linked folder: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/MonetBank/VM/2028-05/scan-pack/CVE-2024-XY89.

3) SLA status: our remediation SLAs are published in our vendor security pack (included in the shared Drive). They are internal policy documented in our SOC2 evidence binder — not a customer contract (unless specifically negotiated).

Next steps: Laura can sign the attestation on letterhead if MonetBank requires. Ben will own the closure tracking for the router exception and Marissa will produce a short weekly update until closure (first update due 2028-06-02).

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Partner Security Manager | Redwood Inference
